Preeminence of Christ
pree-EM-i-nuhns uhv KRYST
doctrinal phrase
From preeminence (Latin praeeminentia, supremacy, the first place) and Christ; the doctrine that Christ holds the first place in all things.

📖 Biblical Definition

The preeminence of Christ is the doctrine that the Lord Jesus holds the first place—the supremacy, the headship, the chief seat—in all things, in creation, in redemption, and in the church. Paul sets it forth in the great Christological hymn of Colossians: Christ is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature; by Him were all things created that are in heaven and that are in earth; He is before all things, and by Him all things consist; and He is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, “that in all things he might have the preeminence.” The word “firstborn” here means not first in time, as if Christ were a creature, but first in rank, the heir and Lord of all. He is supreme as the eternal Creator, supreme as the risen Redeemer, supreme as the Head of His church, and it pleased the Father that in Him all fulness should dwell. The preeminence of Christ is therefore the great corrective to every rival—to the angel-worship and false philosophy at Colosse, and to every modern attempt to set Christ among many teachers, paths, or saviours. The dictionary holds the preeminence as the heart of true worship and right priorities: Christ is to have the first place in the believer’s affections, in the church’s worship, and in the whole created order, for in all things He must have the preeminence.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The doctrine that Christ holds the first place—supremacy and headship—in creation, redemption, and the church, that in all things He might have the preeminence.

expand to see more

PREEMINENCE OF CHRIST, the doctrine of Christ’s first place in all things.

Set forth in the Christological hymn of Colossians 1.

Christ the image of God, the firstborn (first in rank) of creation, by whom all things were made.

The head of the body, the church, the firstborn from the dead.

It pleased the Father that in Him all fulness should dwell.

📖 Key Scripture

Col 1:18 — "And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence."

Col 1:16 — "For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:"

Col 1:17 — "And he is before all things, and by him all things consist."

Heb 1:3 — "Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Christ’s supremacy is denied by religious pluralism, which sets Him among many teachers, paths, and saviours.

expand to see more

The reigning corruption is religious pluralism—the doctrine that Christ is one teacher, path, or saviour among many, all leading to the same God. This directly contradicts the preeminence Scripture assigns Him. If by Him all things were created and in Him all fulness dwells, He cannot be set on a shelf beside Buddha, Muhammad, or the spiritual sages of the age. The Lord Jesus is not first among equals but supreme without rival, the only name under heaven given among men whereby we must be saved.

A subtler corruption arises within the church, where Christ is honored in word but displaced in practice—crowded out by programs, personalities, politics, and self. The preeminence of Christ rebukes this too: He is to have the first place in the church’s worship and the believer’s heart, not a place among many. The dictionary holds the doctrine in its full force against both the pluralism that denies His supremacy among the religions and the worldliness that erodes His supremacy within the church. In all things He must have the preeminence.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word names Christ’s first place and supremacy, the rank that belongs to Him alone as Creator, Redeemer, and Head.

expand to see more

Greek prōteuō — to hold the first place, to be preeminent; “that he might have the preeminence.”

Greek prōtotokos — firstborn, here first in rank and heirship, not first in time.

Greek plērōma — fulness; all the fulness of God dwells in Christ.

Christ is supreme in creation, in resurrection, and as head of the church.

The word stands against every rival claim to the first place.

Usage

"The preeminence of Christ is preached against religious pluralism and idolatry."

"Colossians 1 is the central passage for Christ’s supremacy over creation and the church."

"The doctrine is applied to give Christ the first place in worship and the believer’s heart."
